Honestly, in this situation, yes, you kinda would be the asshole if you started dating your friend’s ex, at least at this point. Let me explain why.

First, it’s a pretty messy scenario—all three of you (you, GB, and HR) are in the same friend group, and it sounds like this breakup is fresh and the group wasn’t even told about it right away. Even though GB and HR broke up and you weren’t the cause of their breakup, dating a close friend’s ex—especially so soon—can create a lot of drama in tight-knit groups. That’s why you’re facing backlash now.

You mentioned that while HR and GB were still together, you were close friends with HR and had romantic feelings for her. Even if you never acted on those feelings until after they broke up, people might see this as you plotting something behind the scenes—or at least, moving in really fast. Three weeks isn’t much time; it doesn’t give everyone time to adjust to HR and GB not being together. That's probably why your friends are reacting strongly.

You say you aren’t trying to cause drama and that breakups should be respected and everyone should move on. While ideally that’s true, friendships—especially in shared groups—require care and sensitivity. It’s not just about your relationship with HR, but also maintaining the group’s trust. If you dive into this new relationship right away, it’s natural that others—especially GB—might feel hurt or even betrayed. 

Also, you said yourself that earlier you didn’t think you were in a good place for a relationship. Is this the healthiest time for you to start anything new, especially one guaranteed to shake up your friend group?

In summary: Yes, I think you would be the asshole if you started dating your friend’s ex right now, given all these factors. If you truly value your friendships, it’d probably be wiser to wait, talk things through with the people involved (especially GB), and give yourself AND the group more time to adjust before moving forward with HR.
